title: 18. Area of a Trapezium and a Polygon

q.t: Which is the formula for the area of a trapezium with parallel sides a and b and height h?
q.e: Two copies of the trapezium fit together to make a parallelogram with base (a + b) and height h. One trapezium is half of that.

q.t: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm and height 4 cm (in cm²).
Find the area of a rhombus with diagonals 8 cm and 6 cm (in cm²).
q.e: The diagonals cut it into 4 right triangles that fill half of an 8 × 6 rectangle: ½ × 8 × 6 = 24.

q.t: Find the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 4 cm (in cm²).
q.e: Base × height: slide the end triangle across and it becomes a 9 × 4 rectangle.

q.t: Find the area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 5 cm (in cm²).
q.e: Half of base × height.

q.t: How many square metres make 1 hectare?
q.e: A hectare is a square 100 m by 100 m.

q.t: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 5 cm and 7 cm and height 6 cm (in cm²).
A quadrilateral has a diagonal d and perpendiculars h₁ and h₂ dropped on it from the other two vertices. Its area is:
q.e: The diagonal makes two triangles with the same base d: ½dh₁ + ½dh₂.

q.t: A quadrilateral has a diagonal of 10 cm, and the perpendiculars on it from the opposite vertices are 3 cm and 5 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
Find the area of a square of side 11 m (in m²).
q.e: side × side.

q.t: A trapezium has area 105 cm², height 7 cm and one parallel side 12 cm. Find the other parallel side (in cm).
Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 24 cm and 16 cm and height 15 cm (in cm²).
A rhombus has area 96 cm² and one diagonal 16 cm. Find the other diagonal (in cm).
A quadrilateral has a diagonal of 24 cm, with perpendiculars of 8 cm and 13 cm on it from the opposite vertices. Find its area (in cm²).
A trapezium has parallel sides in the ratio 3 : 5, height 10 cm and area 320 cm². Find the longer parallel side (in cm).
q.e: ½ × 8k × 10 = 40k = 320, so k = 8. Sides: 24 cm and 40 cm.

q.t: A rhombus has side 13 cm and one diagonal 10 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Half-diagonal 5 with side 13 gives the other half = 12, so that diagonal is 24. Area = ½ × 10 × 24 = 120.

q.t: A trapezium has area 180 cm² and parallel sides 15 cm and 21 cm. Find its height (in cm).
An isosceles trapezium has parallel sides 10 cm and 22 cm, and each slant side is 10 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: The extra 12 cm of the base is split 6 and 6. Height: 10² − 6² = 64 → 8 cm. Area = ½ × 32 × 8 = 128.

q.t: A canal’s cross-section is a trapezium 8 m wide at the top, 6 m wide at the bottom and 3 m deep. Find the area of the cross-section (in m²).
A rhombus has perimeter 40 cm and height 7 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram: base × height = 10 × 7 = 70.

q.t: A trapezium has parallel sides 25 cm and 11 cm, and non-parallel sides 15 cm and 13 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Cutting off a parallelogram leaves a triangle with sides 13, 14, 15, whose height on the 14 cm side is 12 cm (9-12-15 and 5-12-13 triangles). Area = ½ × 36 × 12 = 216.

q.t: A ‘house’ shape is a rectangle 12 m by 8 m with a triangle of height 5 m on top of the 12 m side. Find its area (in m²).
q.e: Split it into known shapes: rectangle 96 + triangle ½ × 12 × 5 = 30. Total 126.

q.t: A hexagon is made of a rectangle 10 cm by 6 cm with a triangle of height 4 cm on each 6 cm side. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Rectangle 60 + two triangles of ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 each: 84.

q.t: A trapezium has the same area as a square of side 12 cm. Its parallel sides are 10 cm and 14 cm. Find its height (in cm).
In quadrilateral ABCD, BD = 26 cm and the perpendiculars from A and C to BD are 12.8 cm and 11.2 cm. Find the area (in cm²).
A trapezium has area 475 cm² and height 19 cm. One parallel side is 4 cm longer than the other. Find the longer side (in cm).
q.e: Sum of parallel sides = 950 ÷ 19 = 50. With a difference of 4: 23 cm and 27 cm.

q.t: Find the area of a kite with diagonals 14 cm and 20 cm (in cm²).
q.e: The diagonals are perpendicular, so area = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = 140.

q.t: The height of a trapezium is doubled while its parallel sides stay the same. Its area:
q.e: Area = ½(a + b) × h is directly proportional to h.

q.t: A floor is covered by 3000 rhombus-shaped tiles, each with diagonals 45 cm and 30 cm. Find the area of the floor (in m²).
A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles by joining its centre to the vertices. Each triangle has area 15 cm². Find the area of the hexagon (in cm²).
q.e: The hexagon is exactly these six triangles: 6 × 15 = 90.

q.t: A trapezium has parallel sides 60 cm and 77 cm, and non-parallel sides 25 cm and 26 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Cut off a parallelogram to leave a triangle with sides 25, 26, 17. Its height on the 17 cm side is 24 cm (7-24-25 and 10-24-26 triangles). Area = ½ × 137 × 24 = 1644.

q.t: A rhombus has the same area as a triangle with base 24.8 cm and height 16.5 cm. One diagonal of the rhombus is 22 cm. Find the other (in cm).
A regular octagon of side 5 m is split into a rectangle 11 m by 5 m and two equal trapeziums, each with parallel sides 5 m and 11 m and height 4 m. Find its area (in m²).
q.e: Rectangle 55 + two trapeziums of ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 each: 55 + 64 = 119.

q.t: The line joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides of a trapezium is 15 cm long, and the height is 8 cm. Find the area (in cm²).
q.e: That mid-line equals the average of the parallel sides, ½(a + b). So area = mid-line × height = 120.

q.t: A quadrilateral has perpendicular diagonals of 18 cm and 25 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: With perpendicular diagonals, each half of one is the height on the other: area = ½ × d₁ × d₂.

q.t: A trapezium has parallel sides in the ratio 2 : 3, they are 12 cm apart, and the area is 360 cm². Find the shorter parallel side (in cm).
q.e: ½ × 5k × 12 = 30k = 360, so k = 12. Sides: 24 cm and 36 cm.

q.t: An isosceles trapezium has parallel sides 12 cm and 24 cm and perimeter 56 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Each slant side = (56 − 36) ÷ 2 = 10. The overhang is 6 on each side, so the height is 8. Area = ½ × 36 × 8 = 144.

q.t: A square and a rhombus both have perimeter 40 cm. The rhombus has height 8 cm. How much greater is the square’s area (in cm²)?
q.e: Both have side 10. Square: 100. Rhombus: 10 × 8 = 80. Leaning the sides over reduces the height and so the area.

q.t: A field is a trapezium with parallel sides 120 m and 80 m, 50 m apart. Find the cost of ploughing it at ₹3 per m² (in ₹).
Both parallel sides and the height of a trapezium are doubled. Its area becomes:
q.e: (a + b) doubles and h doubles, so the product is multiplied by 2 × 2 = 4.
